newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida says strike won't affect operations.
newsitem.headline: Escondida says strike won't affect operations.

text.p: The workers' union at Escondida copper mine representing 17 percent of the mine's workforce has begun a legal strike at the pit in northern Chile but the stoppage won't hit operations, the company said.

"The Union de Minera Escondida and adherents, 353 in total, representing 17 percent of the Escondida workforce, began a strike action 0800 (local/1300 GMT) on April 18," the company said in a statement.
It said 120 members of the union joined the strike as of the first shift Friday. The next shift begins at 2000 local, union spokesmen said earlier.

"Operations will not be affected. Making use of all means established by the law, Minera Escondida will warrant the safety and liberty of work to the vast majority of its employees which are not involved in the process," the company also said in its statement, which was issued in English.
The mine, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc employs about 2,000 workers.
